knowledge:
- key_parameters: <which=Specifies the pathway view: "mixed" (proteins and metabolites), "metabolites" (metabolites only, propagated through proteins), or default (proteins only, propagated through metabolites) ;; species=The species name (e.g., "hsapiens") passed to pathways() ;; database=The pathway database name (e.g., "kegg", "reactome", "smpdb") passed to pathways() ;; Ncpus=Global option options(Ncpus = X) to enable parallel processing for convertIdentifiers, runClipper, and runTopologyGSA>
- alternatives: <SPIA=Use for signaling pathway impact analysis when direction and type of interaction are critical (protein-only networks) ;; topologyGSA=Uses graphical models to test pathway deregulation (means and variances) on protein-only networks ;; clipper=Identifies specific altered signal paths; it is the only method that can handle metabolomics or mixed (gene + metabolite) data>
- when_to_use: <When performing pathway analysis that incorporates topological structure (edges, directions, types of interactions) rather than simple gene set enrichment, or when integrating transcriptomic and metabolomic data into a single pathway analysis>
- pitfalls: <Identifier Prefixes=Since version 1.24, all node IDs are prefixed with their type (e.g., "ENTREZID:7157", "SYMBOL:TP53", "CAS:56-85-9"). User data rownames must be formatted with these exact prefixes to match ;; Parallelism=To exploit parallelism, pass the entire list of pathways to convertIdentifiers rather than using manual loops like lapply ;; SPIA Working Directory=prepareSPIA saves .RData files in the current working directory. If the working directory changes, prepareSPIA must be re-run>

workflows.name: spia_analysis
workflows.intent: Run Signaling Pathway Impact Analysis (SPIA) on differential gene expression data using graphite pathways.
input: top.txt (data frame of differential expression results with probe IDs and logFC)
hgu133plus2.db (Bioconductor annotation package for probe-to-Entrez mapping)
workflows.stages: 1. Map probe IDs to Entrez IDs and format with the "ENTREZID:" prefix ;; 2. Extract logFC for significant genes and define the background gene list ;; 3. Load KEGG pathways and convert identifiers to "ENTREZID" ;; 4. Prepare SPIA input files using prepareSPIA ;; 5. Run SPIA using runSPIA
workflows.code:
top$ENTREZ <- mapIds(hgu133plus2.db,
                     top$ID, "ENTREZID", "PROBEID", multiVals = "first")
top <- top[!is.na(top$ENTREZ) & !duplicated(top$ENTREZ), ]
top$ENTREZ <- paste("ENTREZID", top$ENTREZ, sep = ":")
tg1 <- top[top$adj.P.Val < 0.05, ]

DE_Colorectal = tg1$logFC
names(DE_Colorectal) <- tg1$ENTREZ
ALL_Colorectal <- top$ENTREZ

kegg <- pathways("hsapiens", "kegg")
kegg <- convertIdentifiers(kegg, "ENTREZID")
kegg <- kegg[c("Bladder cancer", "Cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway")]
prepareSPIA(kegg, "keggEx")
res <- runSPIA(de = DE_Colorectal, all = ALL_Colorectal, "keggEx")

workflows.name: topology_gsa_analysis
workflows.intent: Test pathway deregulation using graphical models (topologyGSA) on gene expression data.
workflows.stages: 1. Format expression matrix column names with the "SYMBOL:" prefix ;; 2. Load KEGG pathways and convert identifiers to "SYMBOL" ;; 3. Run topologyGSA variance test using runTopologyGSA
workflows.code:
colnames(y1) <- paste("SYMBOL", colnames(y1), sep = ":")
colnames(y2) <- paste("SYMBOL", colnames(y2), sep = ":")

kegg <- pathways("hsapiens", "kegg")
p <- convertIdentifiers(kegg[["Fc epsilon RI signaling pathway"]], "SYMBOL")
runTopologyGSA(p, "var", y1, y2, 0.05)

workflows.name: clipper_gene_expression
workflows.intent: Identify significant pathways and find the most relevant altered gene signal paths using clipper.
workflows.stages: 1. Define sample classes (1 and 2) based on phenotype ;; 2. Extract expression matrix and format rownames with the "ENTREZID:" prefix ;; 3. Load KEGG pathways and select target pathways ;; 4. Run clipper analysis using runClipper
workflows.code:
pheno <- as(phenoData(ALL), "data.frame")
samples <- unlist(lapply(c("NEG", "BCR/ABL"), function(t) {
  which(grepl("^B\\d*", pheno$BT) & (pheno$mol.biol == t))[1:10]
}))
classes <- c(rep(1,10), rep(2,10))

expr <- exprs(ALL)[,samples]
rownames(expr) <- paste("ENTREZID",
                        featureData(addGeneInfo(ALL))$ENTREZID,
                        sep = ":")

k <- as.list(pathways("hsapiens", "kegg"))
selection <- c("Bladder cancer", "Hippo signaling pathway - multiple species")
selected <- k[selection]
names(selected) <- c("Bladder cancer", "Hippo signaling")

clipped <- runClipper(selected, expr, classes, "mean", pathThr = 0.1)

workflows.name: clipper_mixed_metabolomics
workflows.intent: Perform integrated pathway analysis on mixed gene expression and metabolomics data using clipper.
workflows.stages: 1. Load and clean gene and metabolite expression matrices ;; 2. Format metabolite rownames with "CAS:" prefix and gene rownames with "ENSEMBL:" prefix ;; 3. Merge matrices and log-transform metabolite levels ;; 4. Load pathways and convert identifiers to ENSEMBL and CAS ;; 5. Filter pathways based on coverage of measured genes/metabolites ;; 6. Define sample classes and run clipper with which = "mixed"
workflows.code:
gene_url <-
   url("https://romualdi.bio.unipd.it/wp-uploads/2018/04/Terunuma_gene_expr.txt")
gexpr <- read.table(gene_url, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", row.names = 1,
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

metab_url <-
  url("https://romualdi.bio.unipd.it/wp-uploads/2018/04/Terunuma_metabolite_expr.txt")
mexpr <- read.table(metab_url, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", row.names = NULL,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dexpr <- mexpr[nas_by_row < 0.5,]
iexpr <- cbind(dexpr[,idcols],
                impute.knn(data.matrix(dexpr[,-idcols]))$data,
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
iexpr$CAS <- sub("\\s*;.*$", "", iexpr$CAS)
iexpr[,idcols][iexpr[,idcols] == ""] <- NA
valid_cas <- !is.na(iexpr$CAS)
cas_col <- which(names(iexpr) == "CAS")
cexpr <- iexpr[valid_cas, c(cas_col, seq.int(5, ncol(iexpr)))]

mexpr <- data.matrix(cexpr[,-1])
rownames(mexpr) <- paste("CAS", cexpr$CAS, sep = ":")
colnames(mexpr) <- colnames(gexpr)

fexpr <- rbind(data.matrix(gexpr), log(mexpr))

kpaths <- pathways("hsapiens", "kegg")
rpaths <- convertIdentifiers(convertIdentifiers(kpaths, "ENSEMBL"), "CAS")

filter_pathways <- function(pathways, expr, min_edge_num) {
  node_names <- rownames(expr)
  pred <- function(p) {
    ns <- nodes(p, "mixed")
         if (length(ns) == 0) {
           return(FALSE)
         }
         frac <- length(grep("^CAS:", ns)) / length(ns)
         if (frac < 0.3) {
           return(FALSE)
         }
         es <- edges(p, "mixed")
         mask <- (paste(es$src_type, es$src, sep = ":") %in% node_names) &
                 (paste(es$dest_type, es$dest, sep = ":") %in% node_names)
         sum(mask) >= min_edge_num
     }
     Filter(pred, pathways)
}

fpaths <- filter_pathways(rpaths, fexpr, 10)

pos_indices <- grep("^POS", colnames(fexpr))
neg_indices <- grep("^NEG", colnames(fexpr))
classes <- numeric(length = ncol(fexpr))
classes[neg_indices] <- 1
classes[pos_indices] <- 2

out <- runClipper(fpaths, fexpr, classes, "mean", "mixed",
                  maxNodes = 150, seed = 42)
